title: Decremental String Concatenation
summary: Given an array of strings, perform n-1 join operations where each operation concatenates two strings with an optional deletion of a matching character at the end of one string and the start of the next.
statement: Given an array of strings, perform n-1 join operations where each operation concatenates two strings with an optional deletion of a matching character at the end of one string and the start of the next. The goal is to minimize the final concatenated string's length. Return the minimum possible length of the final string.
constraints: Process words in order, placing each new word at either end of the current string.
When touching endpoint characters match, overlap that one character.
Return the minimum possible final length.
hints: Only the current first and last characters affect future overlap choices.
Map each endpoint pair to its minimum achievable length.
For every word, transition by prepending and appending with a one-character discount when endpoints match.
States with identical endpoints have identical futures, so retaining only their shortest length loses no optimum.
editorial: States with identical endpoints have identical futures, so retaining only their shortest length loses no optimum.

tests.explanation: Append ab with one overlap, then append bc with one overlap, producing aabc of length four.
Appending b overlaps the existing final b, so length remains two.
